title: Warn when another session is already working here, and let a narrowed sprint be renamed

history.detail:
PASS: PASS — round 1. Audited 1d7be4c, main checkout. Sprint file read fresh.

================================================================
THE ENV-VAR QUESTION — CONFIRMED INDEPENDENTLY, AND MORE STRONGLY THAN DEV TEAM COULD
================================================================

You asked for a second look at whether CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID/CLAUDE_CODE_AGENT are genuinely Claude-Code-provided rather than something this framework sets, on the grounds that it is load-bearing for Req 2. I am in a position to answer that better than a grep can, because I am myself a Claude Code session:

    CLAUDE_CODE_AGENT=qa1
    CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID=6f40f6d7-7669-5fd2-a92b-6d69e72ba681

Both set, in my own environment, in a session this framework did not launch. CLAUDE_CODE_AGENT reads `qa1` — my actual role, which corroborates your finding that it matches the agent a session was started with, from a session you did not run. And the session id matches the transcript path this session is recorded at, so it is a real Claude Code identifier rather than anything synthesised.

Your grep also holds when widened: no assignment to either variable anywhere in scripts/ or .claude/. The single non-read occurrence is smoke_test.sh:1215, which sets them deliberately as test fixtures — correct and expected.

Established by running, and by running somewhere neither of us controlled.

================================================================
REQ 1 — NEVER GATES. FAIL TRIGGER NOT TRIPPED.
================================================================

Three consecutive launches of the same role in one tree, with a fake claude:
    launch 1: exit=0  warned  child ran
    launch 2: exit=0  warned  child ran
    launch 3: exit=0  warned  child ran
Every launch exits 0 and the child actually executed — I checked for the child's own output rather than inferring from the absence of an error. Two sessions of one role remain possible, which is the FAIL condition avoided.

Corroborated at the code level: recordRoleClaim's read and write are both wrapped in try/catch returning safe defaults, and there is no throw path that could reach a caller. Best-effort by construction, not by intention.

REQ 1 / REQ 3 — THE BLIND SPOT IS NAMED, IN THE MESSAGE ITSELF. Read cold:

  "...this record only sees launches that went through this script, and only at the moment of launch,
   so a session started another way, or a collision that began mid-build with no new launch, is
   invisible to it. Silence never means 'nobody else is working here.' Launching anyway -- this never
   blocks."

The criterion's exact test is whether a reader could take silence as "nobody else is working here." The message answers that in those words. It also declines to presume the collision is a problem ("may be exactly what you intended... or a genuine collision"), names the earlier session and start time so the reader can check, and states the never-blocks property inline.

This is the fifth chance the sprint file mentions for a comment in this project to get an honesty claim right first time. It is right first time, and it is right in the user-facing text rather than only in a docstring, which is where it actually has to be.

================================================================
REQ 4 — ALL THREE MOVE, THE ORIGINAL SURVIVES, AND THE HASH QUESTION IS ANSWERED WHERE IT MATTERS
================================================================

Ran it rather than reading it. After renaming "Original broad title" to "Narrowed title":
    filename          sprint-1_narrowed-title.md
    frontmatter       title: "Narrowed title"
    registry title    Narrowed title
    registry file     docs/sprints/2-in-progress/sprint-1_narrowed-title.md
    original_title    Original broad title
All three move together and the registry file pointer moves with the file, which is the one that would otherwise strand /sprint-status.

Renamed a second time, to "Narrower still": original_title still reads "Original broad title", not the intermediate one. That is the specific thing the requirement asked for and the easy thing to get wrong.

THE HASH BEHAVIOUR — TESTED, AND THE REFUSAL IS EXPLICABLE, WHICH IS THE CRITERION'S REAL CONCERN. I recorded a QA1 PASS, renamed, then ran dev-done: it refuses, with the generic "sprint file has changed since QA1's PASS" message. On its own that is exactly the refusal the criterion feared nobody could explain — a rename is not an amendment of requirements, and that message says requirements may have been amended.

What makes it explicable is that the rename command says so at the moment you rename, not later at the confusing symptom:
  "Phase, verdicts, hashes and history are untouched. If this sprint already has a recorded QA1 PASS,
   the sprint file's content just changed (the title/original_title lines did) -- the next
   /sprint-dev-done will correctly ask for a fresh /sprint-qa1 look first... This is expected, not a
   bug."
The explanation is delivered where the cause is, which is the right placement and the same principle sprint 27's own Finding A is about. Decided behaviour, tested, and explained in advance rather than diagnosed after.

================================================================
THINGS I WENT LOOKING FOR AND DID NOT FIND
================================================================

The test-only path override is production code carrying a test affordance, so I checked it. It is documented as exactly that, checked first, and correctly noted as "a real launch never sets it." If a production caller did set it, the only consequence is the claim landing elsewhere and the warning degrading to silence — bounded, and silence already means nothing by this feature's own design. Acceptable.

I also checked whether the runtime claims file leaks — a record of session ids and timestamps would be precisely the sprint 22 class. It does not: `.claude/role-claims.json` is named in BOTH .gitignore and .npmignore, each with a comment explaining why, and the only packed path matching "role-claims" is `scripts/launcher/role-claims.js`, the module itself. No claims file exists in this repo's tree either. That is sprint 22's lesson applied pre-emptively rather than found by a later sweep. (My first check reported it packed — that was my own substring match hitting the .js filename, not a real finding. Recording that because I nearly reported it as one.)

REQ 5 / REQ 6 — package.json 0.1.29, one line. ALL SMOKE TESTS PASSED; ALL LAUNCHER TESTS PASSED, 190 OK (up 9, matching the 7 unit and 2 CLI integration tests); verify-tarball.sh PASSED, "Installed 0.1.29 (first install)".

The two problems found and fixed mid-build are both real and both fixed in the right shape: the claims-file test pollution solved centrally in runRoleCli() so no individual test needed touching, and the pre-existing state-diff invariant extended to exclude last_claim the same way history already was, rather than weakened. Neither was papered over and both are the kind that would have shown up later as an unexplained flaky test.

INFORMATIONAL, CARRIED: every allowlist entry other than git and npm remains inferred; the empty-string ownedRepository declaration still falls through silently.

RECOMMENDATION

Ship it. /sprint-dev-done 25, then Pipeman ships and publishes 0.1.29, then `verify-publish 25`.

One note for whoever renames a sprint that already has a QA1 PASS: the refusal at dev-done is correct and the rename command warns you about it first. If you hit it without having read that warning, it is not a bug and re-running /sprint-qa1 is the whole recovery path.
